old_value: For a time I wavered between two plans: publishing the individual grammars and dictionaries first, or first presenting the general conclusions drawn from the research into the individual languages. The latter course has the disadvantage that the reader can check the correctness of the general claims only very incompletely: resources for studying the individual languages must first be created for them, given the rarity and often very inconvenient arrangement of those that exist. But I was deterred from the former course by the protracted nature of the undertaking and the length of time that, given the difficulty of publishing such works, would necessarily have elapsed in the process.
reason: Make the source’s singular reader beneficiary explicit rather than using ambiguous them. Section-wide independent audits are evidence; the new English requires human readability review.

The latter course has the disadvantage that the reader can check the correctness of the general claims only very incompletely: resources for studying the individual languages must first be created for the reader, given the rarity and often very inconvenient arrangement of those that exist.
